excerpt: Organise the day around confirmed access, a clear inventory and a usable first night. Keep essential documents and household needs out of the removal truck.
introduction:
The moving van is booked, the boxes are labelled and the keys are nearly ready. It is tempting to think the hard work is finished. Yet moving day often depends on less visible arrangements: a service lift reservation, a vehicle permit, an access card or a person authorised to receive the delivery.

A useful checklist is more than a long list of objects to pack. It identifies what must be confirmed, who is responsible and what you will do if the plan changes. The sequence below is designed for a household move; adapt it to the building, tenancy and people involved.
takeaways: Confirm both properties' access and management requirements before the van arrives.
Keep an essentials bag and important documents with the household.
Document condition and complete safe assembly before treating the new home as ready.

sections.heading: The week before: confirm the move can happen
sections.body:
Check the handover date and your right to access the new home. Confirm the old home's departure arrangements separately. Do not rely on a provisional transaction date when making an inflexible removal booking. Ask the mover about rescheduling terms and what happens if access is delayed.

Building and community requirements vary. [Emaar Community Management's Emirates Living guidance](https://www.ecm.ae/en/communities/emirates-living/lifestyle/faqs/moving-in-emirates-living/) requires a move-in permit for that community. It is a useful example of why the actual management rules must be checked; it is not a universal permit procedure for every UAE address.

Agree the arrival window, loading location, lift arrangements and any protection required for common areas. Send the mover accurate entrance and contact details. Measure awkward access points and discuss large or specialist items in advance, rather than discovering at the door that the quoted service does not cover the work.

Confirm what the quotation includes: packing, dismantling, reassembly, materials, insurance arrangements and disposal. Read exclusions and any claim procedure. Keep the inventory consistent with the final scope so an extra item does not become a surprise on the day.

sections.heading: The day before: pack for people as well as rooms
sections.body:
Prepare a bag for each person's first day and night, with clothing, toiletries, chargers and essentials appropriate to their needs. Keep medication and any required instructions under the household's control. Put identity documents, transaction papers, keys and payment records somewhere secure and accessible, not in an unmarked box.

Label boxes by destination room and priority. A few clear first-night boxes are more useful than marking everything urgent. Include basic kitchen items, bedding and cleaning supplies that can be used safely. Keep valuable or fragile items subject to the mover's agreed arrangements rather than assuming they are covered by the standard service.

Make separate plans for children, older relatives and pets while doors are open and furniture is being carried. The [pet relocation guide](/journal/moving-pets-uae-home) explains why a suitable contained area and clear supervision matter. Give one person responsibility for household needs so the person coordinating deliveries is not trying to do everything at once.

sections.heading: On arrival: record the starting condition
sections.body:
Before furniture fills the rooms, complete the agreed handover checks. Record existing damage, missing items and any unresolved repairs with the landlord, seller or authorised representative. Take clear photographs where appropriate and retain the written acknowledgement. The marketing photographs are not a substitute for a current condition record.

Check keys and access devices, then identify the practical contacts for building management and maintenance. Confirm that the services required for occupation are working and that any account setup is correctly arranged. The [utilities and internet guide](/journal/utilities-internet-uae-move-in) helps keep separate providers and appointments visible.

Do not use a quick moving-day check to certify technical systems yourself. If there is a suspected electrical, gas or other serious fault, keep people clear and contact the appropriate qualified service or emergency provider. Record the issue and resolve the occupancy implications rather than allowing delivery pressure to decide whether the home is suitable.

sections.heading: During delivery: keep the route and decisions clear
sections.body:
Choose one person to direct furniture to rooms and another, if available, to check the inventory. Mark rooms consistently with the box labels. Changing the location of heavy items repeatedly slows the work and increases disruption, so have a rough layout ready before unloading starts.

Keep passageways and exits clear of packaging. Separate fragile items and tools from areas used by children or pets. Ask the crew to identify anything that cannot be reassembled as agreed, and record it before they leave. Do not accept an unstable item as finished merely because the delivery window is ending.

[IKEA's furniture-stability guidance](https://www.ikea.com/global/en/our-business/our-view-on/clothing-storage-unit-furniture-stability/) says its storage furniture should be anchored according to the assembly instructions. Follow the actual manufacturer's requirements for each product and arrange suitable installation with any necessary property permission. An apparently sturdy chest is not a reason to bypass specified restraints.

If the furniture layout changes, recheck access to doors, controls and essential storage. The first placement is not always the best one, but major decisions should still leave the home usable while you unpack.

sections.heading: Before the first night: make a small part of the home work
sections.body:
Prioritise sleeping spaces, a usable bathroom and the basic kitchen setup. You do not need every box open. Keep safe routes between those areas and put tools, packaging and cleaning products away appropriately. Check that everyone knows how to enter the building and contact the responsible person if something needs attention.

Review the delivery list with the mover and note damage or missing items through the agreed process. Retain receipts and photographs. If a repair or installation remains outstanding, record the next action and appointment rather than relying on a verbal assurance that someone will return.

Over the following days, close the old home's handover and account arrangements, update relevant address records and review the new home's practical issues. Keep changes organised so an internet appointment or missing access card is not lost among decoration decisions.

A successful moving day does not end with every shelf styled. It ends with the household safely accommodated, belongings accounted for and the remaining work clearly assigned. That is a far more useful measure of progress than an empty removal truck.
